newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish city mourns maths student murdered for fun.
newsitem.headline: Polish city mourns maths student murdered for fun.

text.p: The city of Krakow on Friday mourned a brilliant university mathematics student beaten to death for fun last week by youths wielding baseball bats.

Traffic stopped, schools halted lessons and sirens wailed for a minute at midday during the funeral of Michal Lysek, 24, who was attacked as he cycled through the mediaeval university city in southern Poland.
Lysek, who had recently returned from a scholarship at Oxford University in England, managed to crawl home before finally losing consciousness. He died later in hospital.
Police said this week they had arrested two 15-year-olds who had admitted to attacking Lysek, a total stranger to them, after drinking a few beers.

As after similar killings in other Polish cities in the last two years, Krakow colleges and schools called for a silent march against violence. The march, backed by city authorities, is due to take place on Monday.

In the capital this week the mother of a Warsaw Polytechnic student unveiled a plaque to her son, who was shot by robbers he had accidentally seen fleeing down the street. His death prompted the largest march through the city in years.
